claims.claim: The frozen Exp010 deployment-compatible classifier was executed online in Exp011 using live packet-derived non-overlapping 100-eligible-packet windows.
claims.qualification: Applies to the frozen Exp011 controlled-laboratory implementation and feature contract.

claims.claim: Across the nine Exp011 result-bearing runs, the detector correctly classified all 1080 observed windows.
claims.qualification: The 1080 windows are observations nested within nine runs and must not be represented as 1080 independent experimental replicates.

claims.claim: The pooled Exp011 detection confusion matrix was [[360,0],[0,720]], with pooled accuracy, balanced accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and macro-F1 equal to 1.0.
claims.qualification: Valid only for the predefined controlled benign HTTP and controlled high-rate HTTP conditions represented by Exp011.

claims.claim: Per-run and within-condition balanced accuracy provides a meaningful two-class performance measure.
claims.qualification: Each individual run and each pooled condition contains only one true class, so two-class balanced accuracy is undefined there.

claims.claim: Fixed-label binary macro-F1 for the single-class per-run and within-condition groupings is 0.5.
claims.qualification: The value reflects the absent second class and must not be interpreted as 50 percent classification accuracy.

claims.claim: The benign condition preserved service without inappropriate mitigation activation.
claims.qualification: Across B01-B03, 3000 of 3000 requests were transport-successful HTTP 200 responses and no mitigation activation occurred.

claims.claim: The attack-without-mitigation condition provided a successful enforcement-free attack baseline.
claims.qualification: Across A01-A03, all 360 windows were classified as attack, enforcement remained off, and all 3000 requests received HTTP 200.

claims.claim: Model attack decisions triggered actual mitigation in all three mitigation-enabled attack runs.
claims.qualification: Each of M01-M03 contains a model attack decision, action request, one successful activation event, enforcement timestamp, and subsequent observable enforcement effect.

claims.claim: After enforcement completion, all subsequent targeted requests in M01-M03 were application-level rejected.
claims.qualification: 2619 of 2619 requests at or after enforcement completion were mitigation-active HTTP 429 responses, with zero post-enforcement failures.

claims.claim: The 381 HTTP 200 responses observed across M01-M03 demonstrate mitigation failures.
claims.qualification: Those responses occurred before enforcement completion and therefore must not be classified as post-enforcement failures.

claims.claim: Exp011 implemented application-level HTTP mitigation.
claims.qualification: The enforcement mechanism changed victim behavior to HTTP 429 after model-triggered activation.

claims.claim: Exp011 implemented firewall, iptables, network-layer packet-drop, or source-IP blocking mitigation.
claims.qualification: The implemented mechanism was application-level HTTP 429 enforcement.

claims.claim: Mean decision-to-enforcement time across the three successful activation events was 0.002484 seconds.
claims.qualification: Measured from attack_decision_timestamp to enforcement_completion_timestamp; range 0.001708 to 0.003529 seconds and median 0.002215 seconds.

claims.claim: Exp011 timing measurements represent end-to-end HTTP request latency.
claims.qualification: Feature, inference, window-observation, and decision-to-enforcement timings have narrower explicitly defined scopes.

claims.claim: Exact client-process wall-clock duration is independently reconstructible from the archived Exp011 repository artifacts.
claims.qualification: The archived client timestamps support request-span duration, not the independently preserved client-process wall-clock timer.

claims.claim: Archived request-span duration and request latency are reproducibly derivable for all nine runs.
claims.qualification: Request span is explicitly reported as first archived request start to last archived request finish and is not relabeled as client-process wall-clock duration.

claims.claim: All 9000 Exp011 requests were transport-successful.
claims.qualification: HTTP 429 responses in mitigation runs are successful transport exchanges with application-level rejection and are not transport failures.

claims.claim: The mitigation experiment proves that mitigation improves application throughput.
claims.qualification: The experiment was not designed to establish a throughput-improvement claim, only three runs exist per condition, and HTTP 429 processing differs from normal HTTP 200 processing.

claims.claim: Exp011 demonstrates end-to-end online detection and actual model-triggered mitigation under its predefined controlled laboratory conditions.
claims.qualification: The claim is restricted to the frozen controlled-lab topology, workload, model, feature pipeline, and application-level enforcement mechanism.

claims.claim: Exp011 demonstrates production-scale or general DDoS mitigation effectiveness.
claims.qualification: The experiment used a controlled local HTTP workload and does not establish production deployment, Internet-scale DDoS resistance, or generalization to arbitrary attacks.

claims.claim: The Exp011 core results are independently derivable from frozen primary artifacts rather than requiring manually entered result values.
claims.qualification: The Section 8 reconciliation independently reread request logs, victim logs, detector events, summaries, and mitigation states and reproduced the core Section 6 and Section 7 results.

claims.claim: Packet windows and individual requests constitute independent experimental replicates.
claims.qualification: The experimental unit is the run; windows and requests are nested observations.
